Screeching Hallow

Four level 1 adventurers ride into Screeching Hallow, a hill village named for the crows that never stop crying over its rooftops. Something has gone badly wrong here. The alchemist’s cellar has opened onto something infernal, and the dead walk in the cemetery and the old church. Mayor Vexley has shut himself inside his manor. Click a building on the village map to walk the party there, then step inside to fight. The Crowing Raven Inn is the one safe roof left: talk to the innkeepers and their guests to trade, rent a room and pick up rumors. An old shrine on the southwest edge of the village is said to have an unusual guardian. Every place you clear stays safe too: the blacksmith and the alchemist reopen their shops, and the church altar can call back the fallen. Clear the haunted sites, then find what hides beneath the village.

Fights use 5th edition rules on a tabletop grid, in initiative order, where positioning and movement matter. Defeated enemies earn XP: at level 4 each hero picks an ability score improvement or a feat, and at level 5 they gain new class abilities. Each hero has one reaction per round (Shield, Absorb Elements, Counterspell and Uncanny Dodge), and you are asked when one could help. Fallen heroes make death saves, and allies can stabilize them. Hover a portrait for a stat block, or double-click it to open that hero’s inventory; spellcasters can open a spell tab there. Each hero has a race that sets ability scores, speed and traits; change them below before you set out. Cleared places can be searched: each hero’s passive Perception spots what is easy to see, and an active Wisdom (Perception) check finds traps, hidden doors and lost items. Outside combat you can equip gear from the shared pack, and a hero with both a melee and a ranged weapon can switch between them on their turn.

Names fit each hero’s race and gender. You can also type your own.

Tabletop grid: each square is 5 ft. Gold ring marks whose turn it is; click a green square to move. Melee needs an adjacent target; touch effects (healing, stabilizing) need an adjacent ally.
